parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module holds together as one concern: application use cases, their DTOs and one shared ApplicationError, all used consistently. It still fails the rubric, because the rule for turning a domain Task into a TaskOutput is written out three separate times instead of living in one place. That rule covers which fields are exposed, how dueDate is serialized (toISOString) and that status comes from getStatus(). CreateTaskUseCase and ListProjectTasksUseCase each declare an identical private toOutput(task: Task): TaskOutput method. MarkTaskDoneUseCase builds the same object literal inline. If TaskOutput changes, all three must be edited, and they can drift apart. The "project not found" (404) lookup is also repeated in two use cases, which is a smaller instance of the same problem.

violations.message: The private toOutput(task: Task): TaskOutput method copies the Task→TaskOutput mapping that also appears in list-project-tasks-use-case.ts and mark-task-done-use-case.ts. This mapping rule should live in one shared mapper.
The private toOutput(task: Task): TaskOutput method is identical to the one in create-task-use-case.ts, so the Task→TaskOutput mapping exists twice.
execute() builds the TaskOutput object literal inline, a third copy of the Task→TaskOutput mapping instead of a shared one.
